findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the effort table's key vocabulary (bare, `us.`, and `global.` forms, as done for the sampling override table) so Bedrock-resolved ids like `us.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5` match and receive the pinned `effort`.
evidence: Sampling section is explicit: "Add each 5.5 id (bare, `us.`, `global.`) to `_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES`" — the effort section gives no corresponding key-form statement.

build_model_settings receives `resolved` (the full model id); for Bedrock the default/resolved id is the qualified form `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` (bedrock_model.py:22 DEFAULT_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID).

An effort table keyed by bare ids only would not match `us.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5`, so `output_config.effort` would be omitted on every Bedrock call — the primary deploy surface (compose slots + alarm ModelId dimensions).
Plan's stated goal: "to keep the frontier and standard passes at today's depth ... pins `high`" — silently unmet on Bedrock if keys miss.
findings.finding: The new per-model effort table's KEY vocabulary is unspecified: the plan does not say whether it is keyed by bare ids only or also the Bedrock-qualified `us.`/`global.` forms, unlike the sampling override table which it explicitly keys in all three forms.
findings.location: Approach → "Effort, explicit." ("one per-model table beside the overrides pins `high` for Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5")
scenarios: Deployed 5.5 run on Bedrock (compose default us.anthropic ids): effort table misses, no effort sent, Opus 5.5 runs at its `medium` default instead of the intended `high`.
Happy-path Testing item ("a 5.5 Bedrock request carries `output_config.effort`") fails if the table is keyed bare-only.
findings.suggested_fix: In the "Effort, explicit." paragraph, specify that the per-model effort table is keyed by the same three id forms as `_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES` (bare `claude-opus-5-5`, `us.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5`, `global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5`, and likewise for Sonnet/Haiku), matching the `resolved` id threaded into build_model_settings/build_agent_kwargs.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-derive the edit/test inventory for TRIVIAL_DEFAULT_MODEL, DEFAULT_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID, DEFAULT_MODEL and VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL by running find_referencing_symbols on each AND grepping each name as a string (monkeypatch.setattr/getattr/parametrize), and reconcile the result against the five named test files.
evidence: Plan: 'tests: the five files a measured spike showed break (all edits applied, 220 test files that name a 4.x id, a changed constant, or a provider/compose/alarm file run: 24 failures in these five, 3,924 passes ...)'
Plan AC1 bases completeness on `git grep -nE 'claude-(opus-4-8|sonnet-4-6|haiku-4-5)' -- <path list>` rather than on the symbol graph of the constants being changed

Confirmed existing structural references to the changed constants outside the named five exist (e.g. tests/unit/test_verifier_class.py:84 asserts .endswith(VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL); tests/unit/workflow/test_review_output_budget.py:322 LLMConfig(model=DEFAULT_MODEL)); these happen to survive only because the tables are additive and the tests read the constant rather than a literal — a property that holds by luck of design, not by the derivation method
findings.finding: The breaking-test inventory for the changed default constants (TRIVIAL_DEFAULT_MODEL, DEFAULT_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID, DEFAULT_MODEL, VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL) and the per-model tables is derived by running tests and git-grep ('a measured spike showed break'; AC1 is a `git grep`), not by symbol-reference lookup (find_referencing_symbols). The known failure mode of that method is silent omission of call sites that read a constant indirectly (e.g. via class-slot resolution, substring matches, or string-keyed parametrization the LSP does not resolve). I could not independently name an omitted breaking file — the additive-table design does protect value-pinning tests — so this is advisory, flagged on the derivation method alone.
findings.location: Scope → tests bullet: 'the five files a measured spike showed break'; Acceptance Criteria AC1 git grep
scenarios: If any future-equivalent of a value-pinning assertion (like test_review_output_budget.py:73 model_max_output_tokens('claude-haiku-4-5')==_HAIKU_MAX) had instead pinned the resolved default's value, the grep/spike method would miss it and the test would break post-cutover undetected by the named five
A string-keyed reference (monkeypatch.setattr / parametrize on a constant's value) is invisible to git-grep-by-id and to the spike if that path is not exercised, leaving an unpatched assertion
